summary: This note is an overview of the Los Angeles Chargers, a professional American football team in the NFL's AFC West division. It covers the team's founding in 1959 as an AFL charter member, its move to San Diego in 1961, its joining the NFL after the 1970 merger, and its announced return to Los Angeles for the 2017 season. It also notes the planned stadium arrangements at StubHub Center and the Los Angeles Stadium at Hollywood Park.
one_line: The Los Angeles Chargers are an NFL team whose history runs from its 1960 AFL start through San Diego to its planned return to Los Angeles.
key_facts: The Los Angeles Chargers are a professional American football team based in the Greater Los Angeles Area.
The Chargers compete in the National Football League (NFL) as a member club of the league's American Football Conference (AFC) West division.
The team was founded on August 14, 1959.
The Chargers began play on September 10, 1960, as a charter member of the American Football League (AFL).
The team spent its first season in Los Angeles before moving to San Diego in 1961 to become the San Diego Chargers.
The Chargers joined the NFL as a result of the AFL-NFL merger in 1970.
The Chargers played their home games at SDCCU Stadium.
The return of the Chargers to Los Angeles was announced for the 2017 season.
The announced return came just one year after the Rams had moved back to Los Angeles from St. Louis.
The Chargers will play their home games at the StubHub Center until the opening in 2020 of the Los Angeles Stadium at Hollywood Park.
The Chargers will share the Los Angeles Stadium at Hollywood Park with the Rams.
